hero.headline: Looking for something to do? 5 Treasure Coast events for Sept. 11-13
hero.teaser: From a Friday-night 9/11 memorial tribute to a 400-foot Cuban sandwich attempt, live wrestling and a Sunday country show, here are five Treasure Coast events worth checking out this weekend.
hero.body:
The Treasure Coast has a packed calendar this weekend, with options ranging from a community remembrance Friday night to family events, a record-breaking food attempt, live wrestling and music through Sunday.

 For this roundup, the weekend starts Friday evening and runs through Sunday. Friday daytime events are not included.

 Annual 9/11 Memorial Tribute in Palm City

 When: Friday, Sept. 11, 7 to 8 p.m. 
 Where: Peter and Julie Cummings Library, 2551 SW Matheson Ave., Palm City 
 Cost: Free

 The weekend begins with a community remembrance at the 9/11 Monument outside the Peter and Julie Cummings Library. The annual tribute is scheduled to include community leaders, first responders, patriotic music and a candlelight tribute, along with a wreath and rose-laying ceremony.

 The one-hour event is family-friendly and offers Treasure Coast residents a place to gather and remember those who were killed in the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks.

 See event details 

 Family Fun Day and Touch A Truck in Sebastian

 When: Saturday, Sept. 12, 9 a.m. to 2 p.m. 
 Where: Sebastian City Hall, 1225 Main St., Sebastian

 Indian River County families looking for a Saturday morning outing can head to Sebastian City Hall for the city's Family Fun Day and Touch A Truck.

 The event runs for five hours, giving families a daytime option before many of the Treasure Coast's Saturday evening events get underway.

 See event details 

 Bite Into History: The Longest Cuban Sandwich Ever Made in Palm City

 When: Saturday, Sept. 12, 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. 
 Where: L. Cpl. Justin Wilson Memorial Park, 2051 SW Mapp Road, Palm City 
 Spectator admission: Free

 This may be the most unusual event on the Treasure Coast calendar this weekend.

 House of Hope and Old Havana Cafe are teaming up for an attempt to build a 400-foot Cuban sandwich in Palm City. The goal is to top the current 365-foot record set in Tampa in 2024.

 Gates open at 11 a.m., with sandwich building scheduled to begin at noon. In addition to watching the giant sandwich come together, visitors can expect vendor booths, face painting, salsa dancing, dominoes and live music.

 The event also supports House of Hope's work assisting Martin County residents facing hunger and financial hardship.

 See event details 

 CCW Coastal Championship Wrestling in Port St. Lucie

 When: Saturday, Sept. 12, 7 to 9 p.m. 
 Where: MIDFLORIDA Credit Union Event Center, 9221 SE Event Center Place, Port St. Lucie

 Saturday night brings live professional wrestling to Port St. Lucie as Coastal Championship Wrestling takes over Ruby Hall at the MIDFLORIDA Credit Union Event Center.

 CCW promotes the show as an up-close, high-energy night built around live entrances, crowd interaction and in-ring action. The event is scheduled for 7 to 9 p.m.

 Tickets are available through the event listing.

 See event and ticket information 

 A Salute to Kenny Chesney & Other Country Greats in Fort Pierce

 When: Sunday, Sept. 13, 1 to 4 p.m. 
 Where: Summer Crush Vineyard & Winery, 4200 Johnston Road, Fort Pierce

 Country music closes out the weekend at Summer Crush Vineyard & Winery with Tim Boyd's Chesney & Friends show.

 Half of the performance is dedicated to Kenny Chesney, while the other half features music associated with country favorites including Alan Jackson, Garth Brooks and Jimmy Buffett. Gates open at noon and the music starts at 1 p.m.

 Advance tickets are currently listed at $8.50 before taxes and fees, with higher pricing at the door. Organizers note that prices can increase as the show approaches.

 See event and ticket information 

 More things to do on the Treasure Coast

 These are five of our picks from a much larger calendar of events happening across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties this weekend.

 For more local events, visit the Treasure Coast Today events calendar .

 The win capped a chaotic season finale that began Saturday before being suspended and completed Sunday.

cards.teaser: Republican nominee Byron Donalds argues that data centers are infrastructure Florida needs to compete, while Democratic nominee David Jolly wants a one-year pause on construction to examine environmental, health and economic consequences.
cards.body: Republican nominee Byron Donalds has outlined three priorities for regulating data centers: protecting customers from higher utility bills, limiting water demands through cooling systems that recirculate water or use air, and keeping facilities away from homes. His campaign says local communities should be able to reject the facilities.

cards.headline: First Border Collies adopted after Palm City hoarding rescue, Humane Society says
cards.teaser: The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast has placed the first Border Collies rescued last month from a Palm City home into new adoptive families.
cards.body: The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast has placed the first Border Collies rescued from a Palm City hoarding case into new homes, the shelter announced this week. The adoptions come less than a month after Martin County deputies and Animal Services removed 36 Border Collies from a home on Southwest Alligator Street in Palm City.

cards.headline: Fellsmere woman, 75, wakes at 2:30 a.m. daily to feed stray cats, volunteers 60 hours a week at animal sanctuary
cards.teaser: Linn Stewart of Indian River County rises before dawn each morning to feed a colony of stray cats, then spends her days volunteering at For the Love of Paws in Fellsmere. The sanctuary provides free pet food to food banks, veterans, and seniors while caring for animals left behind by elderly owners.
cards.body: Linn Stewart, a 75-year-old Indian River County resident, starts her day at 2:30 a.m. driving through the dark to feed her colony of stray cats. After the predawn feeding, Stewart volunteers 60 hours a week at For the Love of Paws in Fellsmere, a sanctuary for pets left behind by senior citizens who can no longer care for them.
